meta_title: TigerPOD: open-source NFC reader for filament spools
meta_description: Build a desktop NFC reader and writer for 3D-printing filament spools from two USB readers and a 3D-printed shell. Open design, CC-BY-4.0.
og_title: TigerPOD: a CD player, for spools
og_description: Drop a filament spool in and your computer reads and writes its NFC chips. Two commodity USB readers, one 3D-printed shell, no soldering.
og_alt: TigerPOD shells printed in nine colours, each holding a filament spool
hero_kicker: Open-source NFC reader and writer for filament spools
hero_lead: Drop a 3D-printing filament spool in and your computer reads its TigerTag chips: material, brand, colour, temperatures, what is left. Writing a tag works the same way. Two commodity USB NFC readers and a 3D-printed shell, nothing else.
hero_alt: Nine TigerPOD shells in black, blue, purple, pink, red, orange, yellow, green and white, each holding a filament spool
fact1_label: ACR122U-compatible USB readers, one facing each side of the spool
fact2_label: screws, glue, wires or soldering: the readers slide into the shell
fact3_label: of 1 kg spools fit: plastic, cardboard, non-reusable and refills
fact4_label: open design and documentation, free to print, change and share
what_lead: The TigerPOD reads and writes the NFC chips of a filament spool on your desk: two standard PC/SC readers held face to face by a 3D-printed support, driven by Tiger Studio Manager.
demo_alt: A spool dropped into a red TigerPOD, its reader light switching on as the chip is read
what1_text: With one chip on each side of the spool and one reader facing each chip, a chip is always in front of a reader, whichever way the spool goes in.
what2_text: The Pod reads and writes the two chips of a spool together, so the Twin Tag pair stays byte-identical and your inventory counts one spool, not two tags.
what3_text: Read what is on a tag, write a new one, change it and erase it back to blank. A TigerTag is never write-locked: rewrite it as many times as you want.
what4_text: Anything an ACR122U handles, the Pod handles: ISO 14443 A and B, MIFARE Classic, Ultralight and DESFire, FeliCa, Topaz/Jewel, NFC Forum types 1 to 4. ISO 15693 tags are outside its range.
what5_text: Commodity readers over PC/SC, the smart-card standard built into Windows, macOS and Linux. No custom board, no proprietary reader, no driver from a vendor.
what6_title: Offline, and chips get a second life
what6_text: The Pod reads and writes locally; nothing phones home. A used spool chip can be rewritten as a plain NDEF tag (a URL, home automation, a business card) and back into a TigerTag.
shells_lead: The TigerPOD is one idea: two ACR122U readers facing each other, held at the right distance by a 3D-printed support. Both published shells hold the same two readers; pick the one that suits your desk.
mini_text: A redesigned, more compact shell: it prints faster, uses less filament, takes less desk space and routes the cables inside. It reads and writes both TigerTag and OpenSpool (NDEF) tags.
mini_alt: The compact TigerPOD Mini holding a filament spool, one upright reader on each side
orig_text: The first shell, sized for a standard 1 kg spool. Same two readers, same features.
concept_title: The shape is yours to change
concept_text: Only the two facing readers matter; the holder around them is a detail. Redesign it for another spool format or another use, and it is still a Pod. Share your remix on MakerWorld and open an issue that links to it.
build_title: How do I build a TigerPOD?
build_lead: Building a TigerPOD takes a 3D print and two USB readers: no electronics knowledge, no soldering, no wiring.
step1_text: The TigerPOD Mini (recommended) or the original, both on MakerWorld, in any filament you like.
step2_text: Two ACR122U-compatible USB NFC readers from any shop, and NTAG 213, 215 or 216 tags to write on.
step3_text: One reader into each slot of the shell. No screws, no glue, no wiring.
step4_text: Connect both readers to your computer. A 2-to-1 USB splitter makes it one cable; two ports work too.
step5_text: The free desktop app picks the readers up automatically. Drop a spool in.
part_reader_qty: 2, one per side of the spool
part_splitter_qty: optional: two USB ports work too
affiliate_note: Some hardware links are Amazon affiliate links: as an Amazon Associate, TigerTag earns from qualifying purchases, at no extra cost to you.
os_windows: Windows: recognised out of the box, the PC/SC service ships with Windows. If a card-emulation helper driver takes over the reader, remove it.
os_macos: macOS: works with the built-in PC/SC stack, no extra driver.
os_linux: Linux: install PC/SC and the ACS/CCID driver, then make sure the pcscd service is running.
kit_lead: The TigerTag shop sells the electronics ready to slide in: readers carrying the project's official logo, and the splitter. Buying the kit funds the open standard.
kit_note: The kit is the electronics only: you still print the shell yourself. A Pod built from generic parts is the same Pod.
colours_title: It comes in whatever colour you load
colours_lead: You print it yourself, so the Pod takes the colour and finish of your filament: silk, galaxy, marble, glow-in-the-dark.
colours_alt: TigerPOD shells printed in fifteen colours: red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, pink, gold, copper, silver, grey, black, white and glow-in-the-dark
finishes_alt: TigerPOD shells in special finishes: eight silk colours, galaxy purple, marble, two rainbows and three glow-in-the-dark prints photographed with the lights off
colours_more: Every photo in full resolution, and as transparent cut-outs, in the repository
eco_lead: The TigerPOD is the desktop's NFC in the TigerTag system: the same spool is read by the Pod, by Tiger Studio Manager on the computer and by a phone.
eco_alt: The TigerTag system: a blue TigerPOD holding a spool, Tiger Studio Manager on a desktop screen and the mobile app on a phone
eco_protocol_text: The open specification and public registry the Pod reads and writes (CC-BY-4.0, irrevocable implementation grant).
eco_studio_text: The free desktop app (MIT): inventory, printers, and the Pod's home. It drives the readers over PC/SC.
eco_phone_title: On a phone, no Pod needed
eco_phone_text: A TigerTag chip is a standard NFC tag: any phone with NFC reads it, and the mobile app writes it with the phone's own NFC.
eco_sdk_text: JavaScript and Python (Apache-2.0): decode a tag offline from its raw bytes, in your own code.
eco_community_text: Questions, build photos and remixes on the TigerTag Discord.
dev_title: How do I read a tag in my own code?
dev_lead: A TigerTag stores everything on the chip, so reading is the same two steps in any language, with no lookup and no network.
dev1_text: With any NFC library, read the 7-byte UID and the user memory, pages 0x04 to 0x27: 36 pages of 4 bytes, 144 bytes. On the desktop, nfc-pcsc (Node, used by Tiger Studio Manager) or pyscard (Python) drive the ACR122U over PC/SC.
dev2_text: Hand those bytes to the TigerTag SDK. It returns material, brand, colour, temperatures and weight, and can verify the signature. The SDK never touches the reader.
dev_play_title: Test the Pod in the playground
dev_play_text: Both SDKs ship a playground, a small local server and a web page. The JavaScript one connects to the ACR122U over PC/SC and shows live card events: drop a spool in the Pod and watch it decode in the browser.
faq1_q: Can I use just one reader?
faq1_a: Yes. A single chip and a single reader work, but you have to present the tagged side of the spool, and the two chips of a spool are no longer kept in sync automatically.
faq2_q: Which spools fit in the TigerPOD?
faq2_a: About 99% of 1 kg spools, whatever the type: plastic masterspools, cardboard spools, non-reusable plastic spools and refills.
faq3_a: They differ only in memory: about 144 bytes for the 213, 504 for the 215 and 888 for the 216. Any of them holds a TigerTag record; pick 215 or 216 for more headroom. All three work in the Pod.
faq4_q: My reader is not detected. What should I check?
faq4_a: Make sure it is an ACR122U-compatible PC/SC reader. On Linux, install the CCID driver and start the pcscd service. Unplug and replug the reader once, then relaunch Tiger Studio Manager.
faq5_a: Yes. TigerTags are never locked: erase and rewrite them as new TigerTags as often as you want, or turn them into plain NDEF tags for another NFC use and back again.
faq6_q: Can the Pod do NFC work other than TigerTag?
faq6_a: Yes. It is two standard ACR122U readers, so it reads, writes, rewrites and erases anything an ACR122U supports: ISO 14443 A and B, MIFARE Classic, Ultralight and DESFire, FeliCa, Topaz/Jewel and NFC Forum types 1 to 4.
faq7_q: Does the TigerPOD need an internet connection?
faq7_a: No. The Pod reads and writes locally, and nothing phones home.
faq8_q: Do I need a TigerPOD to read a TigerTag?
faq8_a: No. A TigerTag chip is a standard NFC tag, so any phone with NFC can read it, and the mobile app can write it. The Pod is the desktop's NFC: drop-in reading and writing of both chips of a spool.
